children: Archer Aviation (ACHR, Financials), is expanding flight testing for its Midnight electric air taxi as the company takes its No Roads tour to the California International Air Show in Salinas on Sept. 26 and 27.

Midnight recently flew more than 40 miles between Salinas and Hollister, reaching 125 mph and a cruising altitude of 3,550 feet. Each leg took about 12 minutes, compared with more than 40 minutes by car, according to Archer.

The company plans to use the tour to demonstrate routes that could eventually turn hour-long ground trips into roughly 10- to 20-minute flights. After Salinas, Archer plans stops in San Martin, San Jose, Oakland and San Francisco before expanding into the Los Angeles area, Texas and Florida.
ACHR shares climbed 4.8% Tuesday to $5.69, although the stock remains down about 24% year to date.
TipRanks data shows a Strong Buy consensus among six analysts, with an average price target of $11.60. That target reflects analyst expectations rather than a guaranteed outcome.
For Archer, the bigger test is turning demonstration flights into a repeatable path toward commercial service.
The next catalyst is Midnight's expanded flight schedule and whether Archer can continue demonstrating longer city-to-city routes.

title: Archer Just Sent a New Signal on the Future of Air Taxis
